To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The proposed policy of keeping no partitions in memory is a better choice than the previous policy of keeping some partitions in memory.
the previous whole program partitioning method is not suitable and the new method, which is based on minimal safe partitions and cache of frequently executed functions, is a viable solution.

(i) a whole program partitioner is proposed for embedded devices which is based on the new policy of keeping nothing on the smart card; (ii) a new partitioning method is proposed for minimal partitions which reduces their size over previous work; (iii) a caching framework is proposed for frequently executed functions to improve performance; (iv) data partitioning is proposed which reduces memory footprint of data; (v) the proposed method outperforms previous work by 500 times on average in speed
In summary, our research is concerned with
partitioning a program for execution on an embedded device such as smart card.
the design of a tamper-resistant whole program code and data partitioning method for smart cards.
the problem of whole program partitioning for embedded devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is suitable for tamper-resistant partitioning of whole program on smart cards.
the new proposed policy is a better solution than the previous one and it is a viable whole program partitioning solution for embedded systems.
the proposed solution to the problem is the first one which is suitable for whole program partitioning on smart cards.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new tamper-resistant whole program memory partitioning method that reduces memory footprint and improves performance significantly.
a whole program partitioner for smart cards is designed which is able to achieve significant reduction in memory usage and speed-up in execution time.
the proposed method is suitable for tamper-resistant whole program execution on memory-constrained devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of whole program partitioning for embedded devices can be solved in a way such that it is not necessary to keep partitions in memory to guarantee control flow.
a whole program partitioner should take into account the memory footprint and performance of the generated partitions and not just the control flow leakage.
tamper resistance is not a significant overhead for the performance of the program and hence can be used in a wide range of embedded systems.
